correctness.rationale: All maximal geodesics in H_n=K2 square K2 square Kn (n>=2) have length 3 and four vertices, changing each coordinate once. Perfect n-path packing saturates all 4n vertices. Each column must touch at least 2 paths; total incidences=2n forces exactly 2 per column. Nonoverlapping column footprints partition the square Q2 as two disjoint edges (E) or singleton+3-vertex path (T). Incidence graph is 2-regular; paths join like footprint-types. In E cycles, occupied Q2 edges alternate a/b directions along each path, forcing even cycle length; in T cycles the missing-vertex/singleton labels trace a closed walk in bipartite Q2, forcing even length. Conversely any even cycle multigraph, including doubled edges, has a perfect packing by alternating Q2 edge directions and taking the unique intersection of perpendicular footprints. Odd n cannot be perfect, and pairing n-1 columns attains n-1 paths; even n attains n, so gpack=2 floor(n/2). Labeled-cycle exponential formula: doubled-edge components z²/2 and even simple cycles z^(2j)/(4j) imply exp(z²/4)(1-z²)^(-1/4). Independent direct graph/backtracking enumeration n=2,3,4 found optimum 2,2,4 and perfect packings 12,0,720; n=4 incidence cycle-type counts (2,2):432 paths and (4):288 paths, yielding distinct multigraphs 3+3=6. Source script is a finite check only.

value.rationale: The sharp parity obstruction for packing diametral paths in a natural infinite Hamming-graph family, together with the exact realizable column-incidence types and EGF, provides a complete structural classification rather than only a small-n count. It distinguishes perfect packability from the volume bound and can serve as a benchmark for geodesic-packing/graph-decomposition problems.
